name: BEST Robotics Competition
description: The BEST (Boosting Engineering, Science, and Technology) Robotics Competition is an engaging and hands-on robotics competition for middle and high school students. Teams design, build, and compete with robots in a themed game. The competition aims to inspire students towards careers in STEM fields by providing real-world engineering experiences.

name: Carnegie Mellon Computer Science Scholars (CSS)
description: Carnegie Mellon Computer Science Scholars (CSS) is an immersive program that offers high school students a comprehensive curriculum, mentorship, and hands-on projects to develop their computational thinking skills and explore the exciting field of computer science. Through engaging coursework, collaborative projects, and exposure to cutting-edge technologies, CSS provides students with a transformative learning experience that prepares them for future success in computer science and related disciplines.

name: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
description: The International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO) is a prestigious international competition that brings together top high school chemistry students from around the world. Participants engage in rigorous theoretical and practical exams to demonstrate their exceptional knowledge, problem-solving abilities, and experimental skills in various areas of chemistry. The IChO provides a platform for students to represent their countries and compete at the highest level of chemistry excellence.

name: National Honor Society (NHS)
description: The National Honor Society (NHS) recognizes and promotes academic excellence, leadership, and community service among high school students. NHS members engage in various service projects and activities to make a positive impact within their school and local community.

name: The Diamond Challenge
description: The Diamond Challenge is an entrepreneurship competition that empowers high school students to develop and pitch innovative business ideas. Participants have the option to compete as individuals or in teams, working on their entrepreneurial ventures in areas such as technology, social impact, and sustainability. Through a series of rounds, including business plan submission and live pitch presentations, students receive mentorship, feedback, and opportunities to connect with industry professionals.

name: 4H Club
description: Engage in the 4-H Club, America's largest youth development organization, providing a diverse and inclusive community for young people to develop valuable skills that empower them to lead throughout their lives. Through Cooperative Extension programs offered by over 100 public universities, 4-H offers hands-on experiences, mentorship, and leadership opportunities to nearly six million kids and teens. This program welcomes all backgrounds and beliefs, giving youth a voice to improve their communities and the world.

name: ACE Mentor Program of America Participation
description: The ACE Mentor Program of America is a dynamic and award-winning extracurricular initiative founded in 1994 to inspire high school students to pursue vibrant careers in the Architecture, Construction, and Engineering (ACE) industries, including skilled trades. This free afterschool program operates through more than 75 affiliates (chapters) across 38 states and Canada, primarily in metropolitan areas, and is supported by a national office.

name: ACLU Youth & Pauli Murray Fellowships
description: Fellowship and advocacy programs at the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) engaging students and early-career advocates in civil rights, law, and equity (observed on LinkedIn).

name: Adobe Student Internships & Research Fellowships
description: Paid university internships and PhD fellowships at Adobe across creative AI, digital media, software engineering, and product design.

name: Adopt-a-Physicist Program
description: The Adopt-a-Physicist Program is a mentorship program that connects high school students with physicists from around the world. Students can ask questions, learn about physics, and get advice from experienced physicists. The program is a great way to learn about physics and to develop valuable skills.

name: AI4ALL College-Credit & University Summer Programs
description: Nonprofit AI education initiative partnering with top U.S. universities to introduce high school students to machine learning, AI ethics, and social impact.

name: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars Program
description: Paid summer internship program for high school (upper-level) and college students to conduct aerospace and defense research with AFRL scientists.

name: Airbnb Connect & University Internships
description: Software engineering, data science, and product design internships plus Airbnb Connect engineering apprenticeship program.

name: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation STEM & Economics Programs
description: Major philanthropic foundation funding STEM education, minority PhD pipelines (Sloan UCEM), and early-career scientific research fellowships.

name: All American High School Film Festival
description: The All American High School Film Festival is a prestigious event celebrating the creativity and talent of young filmmakers from high schools across the United States. This festival provides aspiring filmmakers with a platform to showcase their original films, animations, and documentaries. Participants have the opportunity to have their work screened in front of a live audience, receive feedback from industry professionals, and compete for various awards and scholarships. The festival not only recognizes outstanding cinematic achievements but also fosters a sense of community among young filmmakers.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship & Internship
description: Provides high school seniors from underserved communities with a $40,000 college scholarship ($10,000/yr) and a guaranteed paid summer software engineering internship at Amazon after freshman year.

name: Amazon University Student Internships (SDE / Business Analyst)
description: Paid summer and co-op internships across Amazon and AWS for undergraduate and graduate students in software development, business analytics, marketing, and operations (active on LinkedIn).

name: AMD Student Internships & Co-ops
description: Paid hardware, silicon design, GPU software, and AI engineering internships and co-ops at AMD for bachelor's and master's students.

name: American Computer Science League (ACSL)
description: The American Computer Science League (ACSL) is a programming contest that challenges students to solve a series of computer science problems. It promotes problem-solving skills, algorithmic thinking, and programming proficiency. The contest consists of several rounds conducted online over the course of the academic year, providing students with an engaging and competitive environment to showcase their computer science abilities.
timing_text: 4 Contest Windows (Oct 19, 2026 – May 23, 2027) + Finals Late May

name: American Mathematics Competition (AMC)
description: The American Mathematics Competitions (AMC) is a series of mathematical contests designed to challenge and inspire students in the field of mathematics. The competitions consist of multiple-choice questions that test problem-solving skills and mathematical reasoning. The AMC provides a platform for students to showcase their mathematical abilities and compete at various levels, from middle school to high school.
timing_text: Annual Contests (AMC 10/12 in Nov; AMC 8 in Jan)

name: American Rocketry Challenge
description: The American Rocketry Challenge is a national competition that challenges high school students to design, build, and launch rockets to meet specific flight objectives. Participants work in teams to apply their knowledge of aerospace engineering and physics, fostering innovation, problem-solving, and teamwork skills.

name: ANN Neuroscience Research Prize
description: The ANN Neuroscience Research Prize is a prestigious and competitive competition that celebrates excellence in neuroscience research. Organized by the Association of Neuroscience Nurses (ANN), this annual prize aims to recognize outstanding contributions to the field of neuroscience through innovative research endeavors. The competition invites researchers, scientists, and healthcare professionals to submit their cutting-edge research findings and advancements in areas such as neurology, neurosurgery, neuroimaging, and neurological nursing.

name: Anson L. Clark Scholars Program
description: The Anson L. Clark Scholars Program is a highly selective summer research program designed for high-achieving high school students interested in pursuing scientific research. Scholars have the opportunity to work closely with faculty mentors at the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center, conducting hands-on research projects in various scientific disciplines. The program aims to nurture students' passion for scientific inquiry, enhance their research skills, and provide valuable exposure to the field of biomedical sciences.

name: Anthropic AI Safety Fellows Program
description: Paid research fellowship at Anthropic supporting students and researchers working on AI alignment, interpretability, and scalable oversight.

name: Apple Student Internships & Swift Student Challenge
description: Global coding competition (Swift Student Challenge) for students 13+ plus paid hardware, software, and ML internships at Apple for university students.

name: Argonne National Laboratory High School & Undergraduate Programs
description: STEM research programs at Argonne National Laboratory (near Chicago) covering energy, supercomputing, and materials science.

name: ASPIRE Internship Program
description: The ASPIRE program, offered by the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL), provides high school juniors and seniors with the opportunity to explore STEM careers in a hands-on, professional environment. Through this internship, students work alongside APL staff mentors, engage in real-world projects, and develop both technical and interpersonal skills.

name: Association for Computing Machinery (ACM)
description: The Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) is an international organization that promotes computing education and research. ACM members participate in programming competitions, conferences, and community events to advance their knowledge and skills in computer science.

name: Bain & Company BEL, ADvantage & ACI Internships
description: Early-stage exploratory programs (Building Entrepreneurial Leaders, ADvantage, CREW) and Associate Consultant Internships at Bain & Company.

name: Bank of America Charitable Foundation Pathways
description: Additional philanthropic youth workforce and nonprofit leadership initiatives backed by the Bank of America Charitable Foundation.

name: Bank of America Student Leaders Program
description: The Bank of America Student Leaders Program is a prestigious internship opportunity that provides high school students with a hands-on learning experience in the nonprofit sector. Selected participants engage in a summer internship at a local nonprofit organization, gaining valuable skills in leadership, community engagement, and project management. Through this program, students develop a deeper understanding of social issues and make a positive impact in their communities.

name: Beaver Works (MIT)
description: Beaver Works is an educational initiative and collaboration between MIT and Lincoln Laboratory, offering various STEM-focused programs, workshops, and research opportunities. It serves as a hub for innovation, providing students with hands-on experiences in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Through hackathons, competitions, and educational initiatives, participants engage in cutting-edge projects, fostering creativity and collaboration in the field of technology

name: Berkeley High School Entrepreneurship Program (BHSEP)

The program is offered by the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley, and students have the opportunity to take classes, participate in workshops, and work on real-world projects.

name: Bezos Scholars Program

description: Botball is an educational robotics program that challenges students to design, build, and program autonomous robots to compete in dynamic, real-world scenarios. Participants learn valuable skills in engineering, computer science, problem-solving, and teamwork as they navigate their robots through a series of challenges. Botball fosters creativity, innovation, and critical thinking while engaging students in hands-on robotics experiences.

name: Boy Scouts of America
description: The Boy Scouts of America is a renowned nonprofit youth organization dedicated to empowering young boys and girls with essential life skills, leadership development, and character-building experiences. The Boy Scouts instill values like integrity, respect, and responsibility while fostering teamwork and promoting a deep appreciation for nature and the environment through various outdoor adventures, community service projects, and educational activities. Participants engage in diverse learning opportunities, such as first aid training, knot tying and lashings, orienteering, and citizenship, all while building lifelong friendships and positively impacting their communities.

The awards celebrate the outstanding efforts of young individuals, aged 13-22, who have shown exceptional leadership in tackling critical environmental issues and creating positive change in their communities and beyond. The program offers a platform for young environmental leaders to showcase their initiatives and connect with a network of like-minded changemakers.

name: Bryan Cameron Education Foundation Impact Scholarship

description: Business Professionals of America (BPA) is a leading national organization that prepares students for careers in business and information technology. Participants gain real-world experience, network with industry professionals, and develop a competitive edge in their future careers.

name: California State Summer School for Mathematics & Science (COSMOS)
description: COSMOS is an intensive summer program designed for high school students (grades 8-12) in California who show an aptitude for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) subjects. It is a hands-on and lab-intensive experience that goes beyond the standard high school curriculum, fostering students' interests and skills in STEM fields.

The contests aim to inspire a love for mathematics and provide a platform for students to showcase their mathematical abilities.

description: Nonprofit offering free college-level courses in iOS, Android, Cybersecurity, and Web Dev plus direct Big Tech recruiting pipelines.

description: Nonprofit community supporting Black and Latinx computer science students with academic resources, mentorship, and Big Tech internships.

name: Congressional App Challenge
description: The Congressional App Challenge is a coding competition where students design and build their own applications. Participants develop their coding skills, creativity, and problem-solving abilities, showcasing their apps to elected officials and the tech community.

name: Congressional Art Competition
description: The Congressional Art Competition is an annual contest held by members of Congress to recognize and encourage artistic talent among high school students. Participants can submit original artwork in various mediums, such as painting, drawing, photography, or mixed media. The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their creativity and express their perspectives through art.

name: Conrad Challenge
description: The Conrad Challenge is an innovation and entrepreneurship competition that encourages high school students to develop creative solutions to real-world challenges. Participants work in teams to identify global issues and propose innovative ideas using science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Through mentorship and guidance, students refine their concepts and present their projects to a panel of industry experts.

name: Continental Mathematics League (CML)
description: The Continental Mathematics League (CML) is a national mathematics competition that challenges students in grades 2-12 to solve challenging math problems. The CML offers a variety of levels, so students of all skill levels can participate. The competition is a great way to test your math skills, learn about different areas of mathematics, and compete for scholarships and prizes.

name: Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition
description: Cooper Hewitt's National High School Design Competition challenges high school students across the United States to utilize design and data to address issues in their communities. The competition encourages participants to create data visualizations that tell compelling stories and communicate important information. Students are tasked with translating complex facts and figures into innovative and impactful designs that address various societal challenges, such as health, racial injustice, climate change, peace, and gender equity.

name: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Education & Ambassador Program
description: Global affairs simulations (Model Diplomacy) and student ambassador programs by CFR for high school and university students.

name: CyberPatriot
description: CyberPatriot is a national youth cybersecurity competition that educates and trains students in cybersecurity principles and practices. Teams compete in simulated cyber defense exercises, identifying vulnerabilities in computer systems and implementing solutions to secure them. CyberPatriot promotes cyber literacy and prepares students for careers in cybersecurity.

name: CyberStart America
description: CyberStart America is a free online cybersecurity training game for high school students. It offers over 200 challenges that cover a variety of topics, such as network security, cryptography, and malware analysis. Students who participate in CyberStart America can develop problem-solving, critical thinking, and teamwork skills. They can also compete for scholarships and prizes.

name: D. E. Shaw Discovery, Latitude, Momentum & Nexus Fellowships
description: Suite of 3-day paid immersive fellowships at the D. E. Shaw Group for second-year undergraduate students exploring quantitative finance, tech, and investment.

name: DARPA Innovation Fellowship
description: 2-year fellowship at DARPA (Arlington, VA) for recent STEM BS, MS, and PhD graduates to explore high-risk, high-reward defense research concepts (observed on LinkedIn).

name: Databricks University Internships

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
description: Prestigious scholarship by the Davidson Institute awarding $50,000, $25,000, and $10,000 to students 18 or younger who complete significant original work in STEM, literature, music, or philosophy.

name: DECA (Distributive Education Clubs of America)
description: DECA (Distributive Education Clubs of America) is an internationally recognized organization that prepares emerging leaders and entrepreneurs in marketing, finance, hospitality, and management through competitive events, community service projects, and professional development opportunities.

name: Dell Technologies Student Internships
description: Paid internships at Dell Technologies across engineering, cybersecurity, supply chain, finance, and marketing for undergraduate and graduate students.

name: Destination Imagination

Students work in teams to solve complex challenges in various fields, including science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM). They present their solutions at regional and global tournaments, fostering innovation and collaboration among participants from around the world.

name: Discover Citadel & Citadel Securities
description: Multi-day exploratory program and datathon/trading invitational pipeline by Citadel for early-year undergraduates interested in quant research and software engineering.

name: Doodle 4 Google Competition
description: The Doodle 4 Google Competition is an annual national contest organized by Google that invites young artists from different age groups to create their own Google doodle based on a given theme. This engaging and educational competition fosters imagination, artistic expression, and technological exploration among participants, making it a highly sought-after opportunity for young talents across the country.

name: Economics for Leaders (EFL) Program
description: The Economics for Leaders (EFL) program is a summer program for high school students who are interested in learning about economics and leadership. The program is offered by the Foundation for Teaching Economics (FTE), and students have the opportunity to learn from leading economists and business leaders.

name: eCYBERMISSION
description: eCYBERMISSION is a free, virtual STEM competition designed for students in grades 6-9. Teams of 2-4 students, guided by an adult Team Advisor, engage in scientific and engineering practices to explore and solve community problems. The competition offers students the opportunity to apply STEM techniques, work virtually, and make a positive impact on their communities. Projects are submitted and reviewed online, and top teams receive state, regional, and national awards.

name: El Pomar Foundation Fellowship
description: Leadership development fellowship by El Pomar Foundation in Colorado Springs preparing emerging leaders in philanthropy, nonprofit management, and public service (observed on LinkedIn).

name: Elks National Foundation Most Valuable Student (MVS) Scholarship
description: Awards 500 four-year college scholarships ranging from $1,000/yr to $30,000 total to U.S. high school seniors based on academics, leadership, and financial need.

name: Emerson Collective FirstGen & Impact Fellowships
description: Philanthropic and venture organization founded by Laurene Powell Jobs supporting education, immigration, and climate changemakers and student fellows.

name: Envirothon
description: Envirothon is an environmental science competition that encourages high school students to explore and learn about natural resource management and environmental sustainability. Teams compete in hands-on field challenges and testing in areas such as wildlife, forestry, soils, and aquatic ecology. The program fosters environmental stewardship and knowledge of ecological systems.

name: Euler Circle Institute
description: Euler Circle is an institute based in California that provides high school students with an exceptional opportunity to delve into advanced college-level courses. With a diverse curriculum, students can explore captivating subjects like Abstract Algebra, Number Theory, Combinatorial Game Theory, Cryptography, and Complex Analysis. Expand your horizons, challenge your intellect, and embark on an enriching educational journey with Euler Circle.

FBLA chapters provide opportunities for students to develop essential skills, explore various business fields, and participate in competitive events at local, state, and national levels.

name: Future Engineers Competition
description: Future Engineers is an innovative program that encourages students to explore the exciting world of engineering through hands-on projects and challenges. Participants have the opportunity to engage in various engineering design challenges, such as designing a Mars habitat or constructing a bridge, fostering creativity, problem-solving skills, and teamwork. The program aims to inspire the next generation of engineers and provide a platform for students to unleash their engineering potential.

name: Future Problem Solving Program International (FPSPI)
description: FPSPI is a non-profit educational program that organizes academic competitions in which students apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to hypothetical future situations. The program offers four competitive components: Global Issues Problem Solving, Community Problem Solving, Scenario Writing, and Scenario Performance.

name: Games for Change Student Challenge
description: The Games for Change Student Challenge invites middle and high school students to submit original games, writing, and artwork into a competition designed to promote social change through creative expression. Participants can work individually or in teams to create games based on one of the year’s themes: Recycle the Runway, Be Ocean Wise, or Stronger and Greener Communities. Winners receive recognition on an international scale and prizes such as games, technology, and a $10,000 scholarship.

name: GATSVI Clubs and Venture Challenge
description: GATSVI Clubs and Venture Challenge is a year-long program that provides high school students with the opportunity to learn about entrepreneurship and to develop their own businesses. The program includes a series of clubs that focus on different aspects of entrepreneurship, as well as a summer Venture Challenge where students compete for seed funding for their businesses.

name: Genes in Space Challenge

Participants can work individually or in teams of up to two students, and they are encouraged to seek mentorship from teachers, parents, or other science enthusiasts. The competition culminates in a presentation at the Genes in Space finals during the ISS Research & Development Conference in Boston, MA, from July 29 - August 1, 2024.

Winning teams receive a trophy and an award certificate, recognizing their exceptional problem-solving skills and entrepreneurial achievements. The GYEC fosters teamwork, creativity, and entrepreneurial thinking among young minds, empowering them to make a positive impact on a global scale.

Students collaborate with mentors from various organizations, completing tasks in fields like coding, documentation, outreach, and more. Google Code-in fosters a supportive community, celebrates young talent, and provides an excellent platform for aspiring young developers.

The award is a great way to learn about OER and to develop valuable skills in computer science, digital media, and graphic design.

name: Habitat for Humanity

description: Engineering and technology internships across aerospace propulsion, avionics, radar, and defense systems for university students.

name: Rube Goldberg Machine Contest
description: The Rube Goldberg Machine Contest is an annual competition that celebrates the spirit of invention and creativity. Participants design and build elaborate contraptions that complete a simple task in the most convoluted and entertaining way possible. Teams showcase their engineering skills, problem-solving abilities, and out-of-the-box thinking in this whimsical and challenging contest.

name: Salesforce Futureforce Internships
description: Global university recruiting program by Salesforce offering paid summer internships in software engineering, product management, sales, and customer success.

name: Samsung Electronics America Student Internships
description: Corporate strategy, customer experience, and engineering internships at Samsung Electronics America (observed on LinkedIn in Plano, TX and US hubs).

name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Challenge
description: The Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Challenge is a nationwide contest that encourages middle and high school students to address real-world issues through STEM education. Students form teams and develop innovative solutions to community problems using STEM principles, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and collaboration skills while making a positive impact in their local communities.

name: Sandia National Laboratories Student Internships
description: Paid technical internships at Sandia National Laboratories for high school students (age 16+) and college students in engineering, cyber, and computing.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
description: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards is a renowned program that recognizes and celebrates the artistic and literary achievements of students in grades 7-12. With a rich history spanning nearly a century, this prestigious competition showcases the exceptional talents of young artists and writers across various mediums and genres. Through rigorous judging and evaluation, participants have the opportunity to receive recognition, scholarships, and exhibition opportunities, fostering their creative growth and providing a platform to share their unique voices with a wider audience.

name: Schoolhouse.world
description: Schoolhouse.world is a transformative online learning platform connecting students globally with expert tutors for free, live, one-on-one tutoring sessions. Founded by Salman Khan, the platform offers personalized academic support in a wide range of subjects. One of its unique features is the opportunity for anyone, regardless of their background or qualifications, to become a tutor, fostering a collaborative learning community where both students and tutors can benefit from shared knowledge and expertise.

name: Schulich Leader Scholarships
description: Awards 100 annual undergraduate STEM scholarships ($100,000 for engineering, $80,000 for science/math) to entrepreneurial high school graduates across Canada.

name: Science Olympiad
description: Science Olympiad is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the quality of K-12 science education by providing challenging competitions and hands-on learning opportunities. Students compete in various science-related events and demonstrate their knowledge and skills in STEM disciplines

name: Scotiabank Velocity & Student Co-op Programs
description: Structured technology, cybersecurity, and finance internships and rotational programs for university students across North America.

name: Scripps Research High School Student Research Education Program
description: Hands-on summer biomedical, chemical, and genomics internship at Scripps Research (La Jolla, CA) pairing high school students with PhD mentors.

name: Shad Canada STEAM & Entrepreneurship Program
description: Prestigious month-long summer enrichment program hosted at Canadian universities for Grade 10 and 11 students focusing on STEAM and social entrepreneurship.

name: Shell Eco-Marathon
description: The Shell Eco-marathon is an academic educational program that challenges students to design, build, and drive the most energy-efficient vehicles. It aims to foster innovation, creativity, and technical skills among students while promoting sustainable energy solutions. Teams from educational institutions around the world compete in various categories and vehicle types, striving to achieve the highest energy efficiency.

name: Shopify Dev Degree
description: Innovative work-integrated learning program by Shopify where high school graduates earn a Computer Science degree while working paid software engineering shifts at Shopify.

name: Sierra Environmental Club
description: The Sierra Club Environmental Volunteer program offers individuals the chance to engage in various environmental conservation activities. Volunteers participate in local and national initiatives, such as clean-up events, habitat restoration, tree planting, advocacy for environmental policies, and educational outreach. The program is open to individuals of all ages, providing a platform for community members to actively contribute to preserving and protecting the environment.

name: Simmons Summer Research Program
description: The Simons Summer Research Program is a prestigious research opportunity for high school students interested in mathematics, physics, and computer science. Selected participants spend six weeks working on cutting-edge research projects under the guidance of faculty mentors at Stony Brook University. The program aims to provide a stimulating and immersive research experience, allowing students to deepen their knowledge, sharpen their problem-solving skills, and explore their passion for STEM.

name: Simons Summer Research Program
description: Highly selective 6-week summer STEM research fellowship at Stony Brook University (supported by the Simons Foundation) for rising high school seniors.

name: Sir Isaac Newton Exam (SIN Exam)
description: The Sir Isaac Newton (SIN) Exam is a physics test offered by the Department of Physics & Astronomy at the University of Waterloo. It aims to encourage the teaching of physics by providing a challenging yet refreshing and fun experience for high school students. The exam includes humorous elements and is open to students from across Canada, the USA, and abroad.

name: Snap Academies (Engineering, Design, Storytelling)
description: Paid summer training academies by Snap Inc. in Los Angeles for community college and underrepresented students in engineering, product design, and storytelling.

name: Snowflake University Internships
description: Paid 12-week software engineering, data science, and product internships at Snowflake for undergraduate and graduate students.

name: Society of Women Engineers (SWE) SWENext & Scholarships
description: Free K-12 outreach program (SWENext) and college engineering scholarships empowering young women in engineering and computer science (listed on Instagram @swetalk).

name: SONY World Photography Awards Youth Competition
description: The SONY World Photography Awards Youth Competition celebrates the creative vision and technical skills of young photographers aged 12-19. With various categories to choose from and expert judging, it provides a platform for young photographers to showcase their talent, gain global exposure, and receive recognition for their outstanding work.

name: Space Settlement Design Competition (SSDC)
description: The Space Settlement Design Competition involves high school students in designing space settlements. Teams participate in designing over several months, creating a 40-page written proposal judged in May. The competition culminates in International Finals at the Center for Space Education near NASA Kennedy Space Center.

name: SpaceX Student Internships & Co-ops
description: Fast-paced engineering, manufacturing, avionics, and software internships at SpaceX for undergraduate and graduate students.

name: Spellman HV Clean Tech Competition
description: The Spellman HV Clean Tech Competition is an esteemed international science and engineering competition that challenges high school students to develop innovative and sustainable solutions to address pressing environmental issues. Participants work in teams to design and present their clean technology projects, showcasing their creativity, scientific knowledge, and problem-solving skills. The competition fosters a passion for sustainability and empowers students to become change-makers in their communities and beyond.

name: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
description: Selective 2-week virtual research internship hosted by Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging for high school students.

name: Stanford ProCo - High School Programming Contest
description: ProCo is a computer programming contest tailored for high school students, inspired by the college-level ACM-ICPC. It offers an engaging platform for students aged 13-18 to explore their passion for computer science. Teams of up to three students compete to solve algorithmic problems within a 3-hour timeframe. The contest features divisions for Novice and Advanced participants, ensuring an inclusive environment for all skill levels.

name: Stripe University Internship Program
description: Selective 12-week summer software engineering internship at Stripe focused on backend payments infrastructure, APIs, and developer tooling.

name: SUMaC (Stanford University Math Camp)
description: Stanford University Math Camp (SUMaC) is an intensive residential program designed for high school students with a passion for mathematics. Participants engage in rigorous mathematical coursework, collaborative problem-solving sessions, and research projects under the guidance of Stanford faculty and staff. SUMaC provides an immersive and intellectually stimulating environment where students can explore advanced mathematical concepts, expand their problem-solving skills, and connect with like-minded peers.

name: Taco Bell Foundation Live Más Scholarship
description: Passion-based scholarship for students ages 16-26 (high school and college) awarding $5,000 to $25,000 based on a 2-minute passion video rather than GPA.

name: TD Scholarships for Community Leadership
description: Awards up to $70,000 for tuition and living expenses to final-year Canadian high school/CEGEP students demonstrating outstanding community leadership.

name: TEAMS
description: TEAMS is a science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) competition that challenges middle school and high school students to solve real-world engineering challenges. Teams of two to four students work together to design, build, and test a solution to an engineering problem.

name: tecBRIDGE High School Business Plan Competition
description: The tecBRIDGE High School Business Plan Competition is a prestigious entrepreneurship challenge that empowers high school students to develop and present innovative business ideas. Participants form teams and create comprehensive business plans, including market analysis, financial projections, and marketing strategies. Through mentorship, workshops, and networking opportunities, students gain valuable insights into the world of entrepreneurship and receive guidance from experienced professionals. The competition culminates in final presentations where teams showcase their business plans to a panel of judges, competing for prizes and recognition for their entrepreneurial endeavors.

name: Technology Student Association (TSA)
description: The Technology Student Association (TSA) is a widely recognized organization that promotes STEM education and offers a variety of engaging activities and competitions for high school students. TSA members have the opportunity to explore areas such as engineering, technology, computer science, and leadership through hands-on projects, problem-solving challenges, and networking with industry professionals. The organization encourages creativity, innovation, and teamwork, empowering students to develop valuable skills for future careers in STEM fields.

name: Technovation
description: Technovation is a global program that inspires and equips young girls to become tech entrepreneurs. Through the program, participants learn to identify social issues, develop innovative mobile app solutions, and pitch their ideas to industry professionals. Technovation empowers girls to become leaders in technology, fostering creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills along the way.

name: Technovation Girls
description: Global free tech entrepreneurship competition empowering girls ages 8-18 to build mobile/AI apps solving community problems, backed by major tech sponsors.

name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
description: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS) is an intensive academic program designed for high school juniors with a passion for intellectual inquiry. Selected students participate in a multi-week residential seminar held at various college campuses. TASS offers a rigorous curriculum focused on humanities, literature, and social sciences, engaging students in lively discussions, seminars, and independent research projects. The program fosters intellectual curiosity, critical thinking, and collaborative learning among participants, providing a transformative educational experience.

name: Terry Fox Humanitarian Award
description: Prestigious Canadian scholarship ($28,000 over 4 years) recognizing graduating high school students for courage, humanitarianism, and volunteer service.

name: Tesla Student Internships
description: Paid internships and co-ops at Tesla in vehicle engineering, battery cell manufacturing, energy, Autopilot AI, and finance.

name: The Aspen Institute Aspen Challenge
description: National youth leadership and civic innovation competition (partnered with Bezos Family Foundation, highlighted on @bezosscholars Instagram) for public high school teams.

name: The BioGENEius Challenge
description: The BioGENEius Challenge is a national competition that recognizes and celebrates the achievements of young biotechnology innovators. Students engage in groundbreaking research projects within the field of biotechnology, tackling real-world challenges and pushing the boundaries of scientific discovery. The competition provides a platform for students to showcase their expertise, collaborate with industry professionals, and make a positive impact on global health, agriculture, and the environment through their innovative solutions.

name: The Coding School National High School Research Program
description: Virtual/hybrid high school research program in AI, Quantum Computing, and Data Science mentored by university and industry researchers.

name: The Coolidge Scholarship
description: Full-ride, presidential, four-year merit scholarship for high school juniors covering tuition, room, board, and expenses at any accredited U.S. college.

name: The Gates Scholarship
description: Highly selective last-dollar scholarship funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation for exceptional Pell-eligible minority high school seniors, covering full college cost of attendance.

name: The Highschool Bridge Building Contest
description: The High School Bridge Building Contest offers an exciting and practical extracurricular experience for high school students interested in engineering, physics, and hands-on problem-solving. This competition challenges participants to design, construct, and test model bridges, providing a unique opportunity to apply fundamental principles of physics while developing crucial "hands-on" skills. Students gain insight into the world of engineering as they create structures to specific criteria and witness their creations fulfill their intended functions.

name: The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) Summer Student Program
description: Competitive 10-week genetics and genomics research fellowship at The Jackson Laboratory (Maine/Connecticut) for undergraduate and select high school students.

name: The National Young Composers Challenge
description: The National Young Composers Challenge is an annual competition designed to nurture and showcase the talents of young composers across the United States. Participants are encouraged to create original compositions, ranging from classical to contemporary styles. This challenge provides aspiring composers with a platform to express their musical creativity and gain recognition for their innovative compositions. Winning entries often receive performances by professional musicians, offering young composers valuable exposure and the opportunity to further develop their craft.

name: The New York Times Student Contests
description: Annual series of writing, editorial, podcasting, and summer reading competitions hosted by The New York Times Learning Network for middle and high school students.

name: The Paradigm Challenge
description: The Paradigm Challenge is an annual competition that encourages students to use their creative problem-solving skills to address real-world challenges. Participants can choose from different project tracks, including science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and social impact. Whether it's designing a sustainable solution, creating an innovative app, or developing a community service project, students have the opportunity to make a positive impact. The Paradigm Challenge provides mentorship, resources, and recognition for the outstanding projects, empowering young changemakers to tackle global issues.

name: The Plant the Moon Challenge
description: The Plant the Moon Challenge, organized by the Institute of Competition Sciences in partnership with the Virginia Space Grant Consortium and multiple Space Grant programs, is an engaging and educational global science experiment and project-based learning challenge. Students, guided by teachers, design and conduct plant growth experiments using lunar regolith simulant, exploring innovative ways to cultivate crops for future lunar missions. With a focus on interdisciplinary learning, STEM engagement, and NASA Artemis-related content, this challenge inspires young minds to contribute to the future of space exploration and sustainable agriculture.

name: The Posse Foundation Leadership Scholarship
description: Identifies public high school leaders and sends them in supportive multicultural teams ('Posses') to top U.S. universities on full-tuition leadership scholarships.

name: The Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
description: Highly selective 7-week mentored biomedical laboratory research program in New York City for high school juniors and seniors.

name: The Summer Science Program (SSP)
description: The Summer Science Program (SSP) is an immersive summer experience for highly motivated high school students with a passion for astronomy and physics. Participants are selected through a competitive application process to attend the residential program, where they engage in rigorous scientific research and exploration under the guidance of experienced mentors. Through hands-on projects, lectures, and collaborative activities, students deepen their understanding of astrophysics and engage in cutting-edge research. SSP provides a unique opportunity for talented young scientists to expand their knowledge, develop their research skills, and connect with like-minded individuals.

name: Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge (JIC)
description: Premier national STEM research competition for middle school students (grades 6-8) sponsored by Thermo Fisher Scientific and Society for Science.

name: Thiel Fellowship
description: Founded by Peter Thiel's Thiel Foundation, awards $100,000 and mentorship over two years to young founders (under 22) building companies or deep-tech projects outside traditional college.

name: Toshiba ExploraVision
description: Toshiba ExploraVision is a prestigious science and technology competition that challenges K-12 students to envision innovative solutions for the future. Participants engage in research and collaborative problem-solving in STEM fields, encouraging creativity and critical thinking. Through this virtual competition, students explore scientific concepts, present their ideas, and have the opportunity to win exciting prizes, fostering a passion for science and technology.

name: TurnUp Activism Youth Remote Internship
description: Rolling remote civic engagement and youth activism internship by 501(c)(3) nonprofit TurnUp Activism open to high school and college students (verified on LinkedIn).

name: Twilio Hatch & University Internships
description: Software engineering internships and early-career apprenticeship programs at Twilio for students and non-traditional tech talent.

name: Twisted Spruce Online Symposium
description: The Twisted Spruce Online Symposium is designed for musicians interested in advancing their skills in music composition and guitar performance. The symposium is conducted virtually in two one-week sessions. The first session (July 12-13) introduces participants to key collaboration concepts through classes and professional networking. Participants are then paired in duos (guitarist and composer) to develop a composition. The second session (August 12-16) focuses on individual consultations and project development.

name: Two Sigma Student Internships & PhD Fellowships
description: 10-week paid summer internships in quantitative research, data science, and software engineering, plus Academic Partnerships PhD Fellowships.

name: U.S. Department of the Navy SEAP (Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program)
description: Paid 8-week summer research apprenticeship placing high school students in U.S. Navy laboratories nationwide.

name: U.S. DOE Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
description: Flagship Department of Energy paid 10-week summer/semester research internship placing college students across 17 U.S. National Laboratories.

name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
description: The U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad is an academic competition for high school students (9th-12th grade) who are U.S. citizens or legal, permanent residents. The competition includes local and national exams, and eligible students have the opportunity to participate in study camps. The rules and eligibility criteria ensure fair and competitive participation, covering aspects such as age, citizenship, and academic history.

name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
description: The U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO) is a prestigious competition that challenges high school students in the field of chemistry. Participants engage in rigorous theoretical and practical exams to demonstrate their knowledge and problem-solving skills in various areas of chemistry. The USNCO provides a platform for students to showcase their passion for chemistry and compete at the national level.

name: UberSTAR & Uber Career Prep Fellowship
description: Paid summer internships (UberSTAR) and year-long engineering coaching fellowships for underrepresented undergraduate students in computer science.

name: United States Academic Decathlon (USAD)
description: The United States Academic Decathlon (USAD) is a prestigious academic competition that tests students' knowledge and skills across various subjects. Participants compete in ten events, including multiple-choice tests, essays, speeches, interviews, and a Super Quiz, which covers a specific theme each year. USAD fosters academic excellence, teamwork, and personal growth, providing students with opportunities to showcase their intellectual abilities.

name: University of Waterloo CEMC Math & Computing Contests
description: Globally recognized math and computer science competitions (Gauss, Pascal, Cayley, Fermat, Euclid, CCC) hosted by the Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing.

name: UPenn Biomedical Research Program
description: The UPenn Biomedical Research Program offers high school students a unique opportunity to engage in cutting-edge biomedical research under the guidance of faculty mentors at the University of Pennsylvania. Through hands-on laboratory experiences and scientific investigations, participants delve into various aspects of biomedical research, including experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication. This immersive program nurtures curiosity, fosters critical thinking skills, and prepares students for future endeavors in the field of biomedical sciences.

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
description: USABO is a rigorous biology competition designed to identify and recognize top biology students in the United States. The competition involves multiple rounds, including a preliminary exam and a semifinal and final exam for top-performing students. Participants are tested on their knowledge of biology concepts, laboratory skills, and critical thinking abilities. USABO provides an excellent platform for passionate biology students to explore their interest, challenge themselves, and gain recognition in the field.

name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
description: USACO is a programming competition that challenges students to solve algorithmic problems. It consists of several online rounds, allowing participants to demonstrate their programming skills and problem-solving abilities. The competition attracts talented computer science students from across the United States, providing an opportunity to showcase their abilities and earn recognition in the field.

name: USA Mathematics Olympiad (USAMO)
description: USAMO is a prestigious mathematics competition held in the United States. It focuses on challenging mathematical problems that require deep mathematical reasoning and proof-writing skills. The competition consists of a series of exams conducted in person, allowing top math students to showcase their problem-solving abilities and mathematical creativity.

name: USA Physics Olympiad (USAPhO)
description: The United States Physics Olympiad (USAPhO) is a prestigious physics competition that challenges high school students to showcase their physics knowledge and problem-solving skills. Participants compete in a series of exams covering various areas of physics, such as mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, and modern physics. USAPhO provides a platform for passionate physics students to test their understanding, demonstrate their abilities, and potentially qualify for the U.S. Physics Team. Successful participants may have the chance to represent the United States at international physics competitions, making USAPhO an exciting opportunity for aspiring physicists to gain recognition in the field.

name: USAMTS (USA Mathematical Talent Search)
description: USAMTS is a prestigious mathematics competition conducted over several months, challenging high school students to solve complex math problems independently. Participants receive a set of problems every month and submit their solutions for evaluation. USAMTS fosters problem-solving skills, creativity, and mathematical thinking in a self-paced and rigorous environment, providing an opportunity for students to showcase their mathematical talent at a national level.

name: Vans Custom Culture Art Competition
description: Vans Custom Culture is an annual art competition that empowers high school students to unleash their creativity and design custom Vans shoes. Students are encouraged to express their unique style, artistic vision, and cultural influences through their shoe designs. The competition not only provides a platform for young artists to showcase their talent but also supports arts education by awarding grants to schools.

name: VCU High-School Programming Contest
description: The High School Programming Contest, held at VCU's College of Engineering East Hall, offers high school students in grades 10-12 the opportunity to enhance their Java or Python programming skills while collaborating with teammates to solve programming problems within a three-hour timeframe.

name: Vector Institute Postgraduate AI Scholarship
description: Merit-based AI scholarships ($17,500) and research internships at Toronto's Vector Institute for students pursuing AI-related master's programs in Ontario.

name: VEX Robotics
description: VEX Robotics offers an engaging and competitive platform for students to explore the field of robotics. Participants design, build, and program robots using the VEX Robotics system to compete in exciting challenges and tournaments. The program encourages creativity, problem-solving, and teamwork as students strategize, collaborate, and innovate to achieve success. VEX Robotics provides a hands-on learning experience that combines STEM concepts with practical application.

name: Visa Student Internships & Leadership Program
description: Global summer internships at Visa covering software engineering, cybersecurity, product, and data analytics.

name: Walton Family Foundation Education & Conservation Programs
description: Major philanthropic foundation funding K-12 STEM/education initiatives and environmental conservation fellowships across the U.S.

name: Wharton Data Science Academy
description: The Wharton Data Science Academy is an immersive extracurricular program that offers students the opportunity to explore the field of data science and its applications in business and finance. Participants engage in hands-on learning experiences, gaining practical skills in data analysis, machine learning, and statistical modeling. Through interactive coursework, case studies, and industry projects, students develop a deep understanding of data-driven decision-making and its impact on various industries.

name: Wharton Future of the Business World Program
description: The Wharton Future of the Business World Program is an immersive summer experience designed for high school students who aspire to explore the dynamic world of business and economics. Hosted by the prestigious Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, this program provides an unparalleled opportunity to engage with top faculty and industry leaders while delving into real-world business challenges and opportunities.

name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
description: The Wharton Global High School Investment Competition is an esteemed finance and investment challenge for high school students. Participants form investment teams and manage a virtual portfolio, making strategic investment decisions and analyzing market trends. The competition allows students to gain hands-on experience in finance, economics, and investment management, honing their analytical and decision-making skills in a simulated investment environment.

name: Wharton Leadership in the Business World Program
description: The Wharton Leadership in the Business World Program is a prestigious and immersive summer program offered by the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. It provides high school students with an opportunity to gain valuable insights into the world of business and develop essential leadership skills. Participants in the Wharton Leadership in the Business World Program engage in rigorous coursework, real-world case studies, and hands-on learning.

name: World Historian Student Essay Competition
description: The World Historian Student Essay Competition is an annual competition that invites high school students to showcase their historical research and writing skills. Participants are encouraged to explore various historical topics and submit original essays that demonstrate critical thinking, analytical skills, and a deep understanding of historical events and themes. The competition provides a platform for students to engage with the discipline of history and gain recognition for their scholarly work.

name: World Series of Innovation (WSI)
description: World Series of Innovation (WSI) is an innovation competition hosted by NFTE (Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship) aimed at young innovators aged 11 to 24. Participants pick a challenge, brainstorm ideas, and submit their innovative solutions. The competition encourages creativity, problem-solving, and entrepreneurship skills.

name: World Wildlife Fund (WWF) Student Internships
description: Remote and DC-based internships at WWF in conservation, environmental policy, and livestream fundraising (observed on LinkedIn).

name: Yale DHSRI High School Investment Competition
description: The Yale DHSRI High School Investment Competition, hosted by the Dwight Hall Socially Responsible Investment Fund at Yale University, invites high school students in grades 9-12 to engage in a simulated investment challenge. In teams of 2-4, students manage a virtual portfolio of $100,000, integrating socially responsible investment principles and addressing ESG themes. The competition fosters financial literacy, sustainable investing, and strategic thinking, culminating in a final investment report that showcases participants' strategies and learning process.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
description: Yale Young Global Scholars is an academic enrichment program that offers intensive summer courses to exceptional high school students from around the world. Participants engage in rigorous academic coursework, interact with renowned Yale faculty, and collaborate with peers to explore global issues and develop leadership skills.

name: Young Authors Writing Competition
description: The Young Authors Writing Competition is a creative writing contest that encourages young writers to showcase their literary talents. Participants have the opportunity to submit their original works of fiction, poetry, or creative non-fiction. This competition aims to foster a love for writing, nurture imagination, and recognize outstanding literary achievements among young authors.

name: Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition
description: The Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition is a global initiative that empowers young entrepreneurs to showcase their innovative business ideas and projects focused on addressing pressing social and environmental challenges. This competition encourages youth from around the world to develop creative solutions that contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Participants have the opportunity to receive mentorship, gain international recognition, access funding opportunities, and join a global network of like-minded changemakers committed to driving positive change through entrepreneurship.

name: Youth Volunteer Corps (YVC)
description: Youth Volunteer Corps (YVC) is a national network of youth volunteer programs that provides opportunities for young people to make a difference in their communities through various service projects. Participants engage in hands-on volunteering, leadership development, and social activities.
